title: Requirements for a Test Rig to Investigate Planet Carrier Bearing Ring Creep in Wind Turbine Gearboxes
content:
Gearbox failures in wind turbines (WT) result in high repair costs and yield loss due to long downtimes. Most gearbox damage is caused by bearing failures. A common root cause for damage in WTs is ring creep that is triggered by large deformations in the drivetrain. The large deformations result from the reduced stiffnesses of drivetrain components as a result of lightweight design as a measure to increase drivetrain torque density. In WT-gearboxes, the up-wind planet carrier bearing (PCB) is susceptible to ring creep. Ring creep can trigger adhesive and abrasive wear as well as tribocorrosion. All of those can cause severe damage in the gearbox and in the worst-case lead to gearbox failure.
Although ring creep in small bearings (D < 500 mm) is a well-researched topic, the dependency of ring creep on the system design and the fact that the results from research on small bearings can hardly be transferred to bigger scales present new challenges in the development of new WTs. 
Addressing ring creep in WTs at an early development stage requires a dedicated test rig that can isolate and regulate the ring creep mechanisms while enabling time-efficient testing considering the system’s stiffness. This work presents a new concept for a planet carrier bearing ring creep test rig that meets the specific requirements of realistic and efficient testing.
